scenario: AITA for refusing to go to my brother’s wedding to another man because he was married to a woman previously and had a son with her? | Okay so stay with me. I’m 25 now and my older brother Chris got married when he was 27 to Taylor. Him and Taylor had a son the following year. They seemed to have a really good marriage but around when their son was 3, something happened. They spent a lot less time together and they eventually got a divorce. Well it came out that my brother confessed to Taylor that he was gay and had been “having feelings for another man.” They divorced after this and my brother started a new relationship with this man. This was three years ago and now Chris is marrying this same guy. The thing is, I’ve been witness to the devastation that this caused to his ex wife and son. He still is around for his son, but starting a life with a woman when he never was interested in women is something I’ll never understand. It’s not as if any of us would judge him for being gay. I’ve tried to help out with my nephew when I can so I’ve seen the confusion it’s caused him and the hurt it caused his ex, one of the kindest people I know. Now that he’s getting married again, the invitations have gone out and I’m invited. I really don’t feel like celebrating the harm that he caused his family by going to his wedding. I called him when I got the invitation and explained this to him and he started crying and saying that I wasn’t being fair and that he wants me to be there. I just explained that I couldn’t be there after everything that happened and I hung up. My sister called me and said that I was being an unfair dick and that I need to apologize to Chris and plan to be at the wedding. I told her what I told him. AITA for refusing to go? I think I’m being reasonable but my judgement is also clouded. Be honest.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to refuse to go to my brother's wedding because of what happened in the past. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My brother Chris got married to Taylor when he was 27. They had a son together, and it seemed like a really good marriage at first. But when their son was around 3 years old, things started to fall apart. They spent a lot less time together, and eventually, they got a divorce. It turned out that Chris confessed to Taylor that he was gay and had been having feelings for another man. After the divorce, Chris started a new relationship with this man, and now he's getting married to him. I've been witness to the devastation this caused to Taylor and their son. Even though Chris is still around for his son, starting a life with a woman when he was never really interested in women is something I can't understand. It's not like any of us would judge him for being gay. I've tried to help out with my nephew when I can, and I've seen the confusion it's caused him and the hurt it's caused his ex, who is one of the kindest people I know. Now that Chris is getting married again, the invitations have gone out, and I was invited. I really don't feel like celebrating the harm that he caused his family by going to his wedding. I called him when I got the invitation and explained this to him, and he started crying and said I wasn't being fair and that he wants me there. I just explained that I couldn't be there after everything that happened and hung up. My sister called me and said I was being an unfair dick and that I need to apologize to Chris and plan to be at the wedding. I told her what I told him. Now I'm wondering if I'm being AITA (Are You Acting In The Best Interest Of The Relationship) for refusing to go. I think I'm being reasonable, but my judgment is also clouded. So, is it right or wrong for me to refuse to go to my brother's wedding? I need to think about this carefully. First, I need to consider the reasons behind my decision. I'm hurt and upset because of the pain Chris caused to our family, especially to Taylor and the nephew. I don't feel comfortable celebrating his new marriage because of the past hurt. Is that a valid reason to refuse attending? On the other hand, my sister thinks I'm being unfair and wants me to apologize and attend. She might believe that family should support each other, especially on such an important occasion as a wedding. But I'm struggling with the emotional impact of Chris's past actions. I also need to think about the potential consequences of my decision. If I don't attend, how will that affect my relationship with Chris and my sister? Will it cause more conflict or distance between us? Or is it better to stand my ground and prioritize my own feelings and the well-being of the family? Another aspect to consider is whether attending the wedding would help in healing the family or if it would just pretend that everything is okay when it's not. Maybe it's better to address the issues directly rather than attending the wedding without resolving the underlying problems. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could send a gift or a card instead of attending in person. That way, I'm showing support without being physically present. But I'm not sure if that would be acceptable to Chris or if it would make things better or worse. Additionally, I need to reflect on my own feelings and boundaries. Am I being too rigid, or am I standing up for what I believe is right? It's important to respect my own emotions and not feel pressured to attend just to please others. In summary, I'm torn between supporting my brother on his wedding day and respecting my own feelings and the hurt caused by his past actions. I need to weigh the pros and cons, consider the impact on my relationships, and decide what aligns best with my values and well-being.
